links.outcome: Radiation dose, operation time and complications with generative AI low-dose DSA versus standard protocols in RCT
links.effect: AK 151.3 vs 457.4 mGy (P<0.001); DAP 4009.7 vs 12531.6 μGy m2; operation time 34.8 vs 33.1 min; complications 7.5% vs 8.1% (noninferior).
links.quote: The GenDSA-V2 group showed substantially reduced radiation exposure, with an air kerma (AK) of 151.3 ± 125.1 mGy compared to 457.4 ± 407.4 mGy in the standard clinical protocols (SCP) group (mean difference = -306.1 mGy, 95% confidence interval (CI) = -342.3 to -269.9, P < 0.001 for superiority) and a dose-area product (DAP) of 4009.7 ± 2767.9 μGy m<sup>2</sup> versus 12531.6 ± 9145.9 μGy m<sup>2</sup> (mean difference = -8521.9 μGy m<sup>2</sup>, 95% CI = -9333.1 to -7710.7, P < 0.001 for superiority).

screen.reason: Prospective randomized controlled trial testing the clinical deployment of a generative AI-based low-dose digital subtraction angiography (DSA) system during actual operations to reduce radiation dose.
